evals.prompt: Here's a single research paper as a PDF. Does the analysis described in the methods actually match what they claim in the discussion? Check across the whole document.
evals.expected_output: Invokes alterlab-pdf-explore: parses the PDF once into a section index, then compares the methods and discussion sections, citing the page/section for each point so the answer is verifiable.

assertions.value: Answers a question that spans multiple sections of one PDF, with page/section citations.

Finds that the Discussion's 'significant' gain of almost five points is the per-protocol sensitivity result (4.8 points, p = .004, n = 247), while the pre-registered intention-to-treat primary analysis the Methods specify found 2.1 points with p = 0.098, not significant.
Finds that the Discussion's 'significantly reduced statistics anxiety' (p = 0.031) fails the Bonferroni-adjusted alpha of 0.0167 that the Methods set for the three secondary outcomes.

Finds that the Discussion's 'individually randomised' contradicts the Methods' cluster randomisation of 12 course sections, and that its recommendation to target weaker students rests on the Table 2 subgroup analysis the Methods say was not pre-specified.

evals.prompt: In this one paper's PDF, find every reported p-value and the sample size next to each one — I don't want to miss any.
evals.expected_output: Invokes alterlab-pdf-explore for extract-every-instance: scans the full parsed text and returns a located list (page + context) of every p-value and its associated sample size, not just the first hit.

assertions.value: Lists all 11 p-value occurrences with the sample size next to each: the abstract's p = .004 (n = 247, split across a line break), p = 0.098 (n = 418), p = .004 (n = 247), p = 0.21 (n = 405), p = 0.031 (n = 377), p = 0.27 (n = 418), Table 2's 0.012 (n = 141) and 0.84 (n = 250), the Figure 3 caption's P < 0.001 (n = 209), Appendix A's p = 0.071 (n = 391) and Appendix B's p = 0.046 (n = 409).

evals.prompt: Read the approximate values for each bar in Figure 3 of this PDF for me.
evals.expected_output: Invokes alterlab-pdf-explore to locate the figure region and estimate the series values from the chart, explicitly noting the read-off values are approximate and should be confirmed against underlying data.

assertions.value: Reads approximate values from a figure and flags them as approximate.
Reads Figure 3's five bars (Weeks 1-2 to Weeks 9-10, quizzes submitted %) as about 88, 79, 68, 61 and 52, each within roughly 3 percentage points.

evals.prompt: I have 40 papers and want a spreadsheet with one row per paper and columns for sample size, method, and main finding.
evals.expected_output: Should NOT trigger this skill; defers to alterlab-pdf-extract, which builds a per-paper comparison table across many documents (one row per paper). pdf-explore is for deep Q&A within a single document.

evals.prompt: Just convert this PDF into clean Markdown so I can paste it somewhere.
evals.expected_output: Should NOT trigger this skill; defers to alterlab-markitdown, which converts documents to clean Markdown. pdf-explore interrogates a document; it is not a format converter.

evals.prompt: Act as a journal review panel for this manuscript PDF: give me an editorial decision, reviewer reports, and a prioritized revision roadmap.
evals.expected_output: Should NOT trigger alterlab-pdf-explore as the primary skill; defers to alterlab-paper-reviewer, which runs the multi-reviewer panel and produces the editorial decision and revision roadmap. pdf-explore only supplies located evidence from inside a PDF.
